chapters.hl-open: Headlines: ChatGPT search, AI fake calls and more
chapters.sd-open: Signal of the Day: how much revenue compute eats
chapters.wp-open: What People Are Saying: four quotes
chapters.ms-open: Money Signal: Binance, tokenized stocks, stablecoin draft
chapters.tt-open: Try This: a familiar voice calls for help
chapters.nd-open: Noise of the Day: Steam review backlog
chapters.tk-main: Sola's Take: the compute bill matters most

ftct.text: This is Tech Signal, where we pick today's real signal out of all the noise.

ao43.text: Today's topic: a filing Anthropic updated ahead of its IPO, and the compute bill inside it.

qmon.text: Wait, revenue keeps rising but losses got bigger? So where's the money going?

8vau.text: Start with search? We all use it.

iz00.text: OK. According to The Verge, OpenAI said this Monday that ChatGPT's search volume is already one fifth of Google's.

rzxg.text: See how it counts: one search only when your question triggers a web search.

a5i8.text: What if I ask what a word means?

cqwh.text: Doesn't count. Definitions and simple how-tos aren't counted.

g62g.text: And OpenAI didn't say where its Google number comes from.

2p4c.text: Its own claim, then. Question mark.

srca.text: Right. The Verge offers a comparison: in court in 2023, Microsoft's CEO said Bing had tried for over a decade and had about 3 percent share.

f46p.text: Bigger search means ads next, right?

we58.text: Yes. OpenAI said last month that ChatGPT ads will start showing images of sponsored products.

ahuo.text: Our advice: when you search in ChatGPT, check which part is the answer and which part is an ad.

kcmm.text: From AI that finds things to AI that fakes people.

2tqk.text: Google yesterday announced an anti-scam program for Asia-Pacific, and one part is Android scam call detection.

a9go.text: Someone uses AI to pose as someone else and calls you. This spots those calls.

j1c6.text: Scam detection built into Pixel phones can also flag suspicious content in common messaging apps.

3myb.text: Also, Google's charity arm is giving $6 million for scam education in Asia-Pacific.

f8zx.text: You said Pixel. What about other phones?

b0xe.text: Google says, with partners, more Android phones get it later this year.

wul6.text: Which models and which regions, Google's post doesn't list.

z2ua.text: Next, Apple. According to TechCrunch, Apple told developers Monday that apps with dating or romance features must all be rated 18+.

r9kk.text: Aren't dating apps for adults anyway?

90kq.text: TechCrunch says so too. The bigger deal is AI companion apps.

ycjs.text: The kind where you set up an AI friend, even a partner, often aimed at young people.

0klx.text: From the 16th, developers must add new content descriptions so ratings match features.

4foc.text: TechCrunch says the popular AI companion apps had 220 million downloads worldwide by last summer.

69ke.text: So kids with iPhones are safe now?

zt5n.text: Not yet. The report doesn't say how Apple will enforce it.

koo0.text: Speaking of AI companions, a deeper question: how do you know which AI you're talking to?

vrac.text: Isn't it the one it says it is?

nnfb.text: Not always. Anthropic says a middle service may swap models to save money, or someone may alter output.

9aan.text: It released an open-source prototype, FlashProve, using cryptography to prove answers come from that model without revealing its internals.

lux8.text: On one GPU, it proves about 110 tokens per second.

t9dy.text: For a 1,000-plus token answer, the proof is about 19 MB.

prva.text: Not yet. It's a research prototype; TechCrunch says no lab plans to deploy it yet.

mktx.text: Another approach is watermarks. Anthropic said yesterday that text from three Claude models carries an AI watermark.

86yq.text: So teachers get a tool to catch AI homework?

m7jx.text: Not so fast. Only on the platforms it lists; and Sonnet 4.6 may not carry it when developers change certain generation settings.

zmrr.text: So no watermark doesn't mean it wasn't AI.

68un.text: From proving AI to guarding from AI.

52k2.text: GitBook, where many crypto projects keep docs, says Monday night someone used an AI agent to attack it

e7fb.text: and got credentials to some systems.

escy.text: How is an AI agent different from a chatbot?

1klv.text: A chatbot only answers; an agent operates software step by step, with less human oversight.

d67c.text: Possibly API tokens, the keys that let programs connect automatically;

5g0v.text: plus questions users asked GitBook's AI helper.

pngi.text: GitBook revoked customer API tokens and told them to rotate related tokens and keys.

14fs.text: It says there's no evidence the content was altered.

54rb.text: Not yet. If your team uses GitBook, rotate your tokens as it says.

s4je.text: OK, something lighter. Lots of us open Netflix at night and scroll forever.

ypdj.text: Netflix on TV is adding an AI Discover tab, and its first experiment recommends by theme.

h2mc.text: Like something light, family movie night, or quick.

jfmp.text: But for now it's US only, rolling out slowly to members using English on supported TVs.

ix3p.text: Maybe not soon. It's an experiment; the report doesn't say when it expands.

4fv9.text: For every 100 dollars Anthropic earns, that much goes to compute.

rtif.text: Over half? What's left for it?

jxon.text: That's today's topic: what's left isn't enough, so it's still losing money.

exb7.text: So who's taking the money? Let's start with one person.

zgw5.text: Picture yourself as an analyst watching new IPOs.

n1w1.text: This Monday, an alert pops up: Anthropic filed an update to its S-1.

otil.text: Before a company first lists its shares, the IPO, it files this document, and it includes the financials.

026w.text: Yes, just the week before. The old one ran to the end of June; the new one adds a quarter, to September 30.

xpmb.text: TechCrunch says that closer to the IPO, Anthropic finally revealed a bit more: how much of its revenue compute eats up.

ig49.text: In plain words: compute means the computers running AI?

jry6.text: Pretty much. Training models, and each time you ask Claude a question, the computing behind it all counts.

bo1b.text: OK, open the filing. First number?

gnzv.text: Up almost 50 percent in a quarter. Nice.

6y9t.text: But read further: the operating loss grew too.

96it.text: That's what I asked: where'd the money go?

c6qv.text: TechCrunch didn't give the loss figure, but named one main cause: rising compute costs.

7nny.text: Remember the signal number? Last quarter, compute ate 48 percent of revenue.

y11g.text: Up ten points in a quarter.

tt6k.text: In dollars, this quarter's compute bill was $10 billion.

bmua.text: No. Half was bought on short-term contracts.

eu8k.text: The filing says that costs far more than multiyear deals.

bs8p.text: TechCrunch's reading: demand grew so fast it had to find compute quickly and pay more.

pcca.text: The filing also has a chart: how much revenue each dollar of compute brings back.

mex6.text: Up since early 2025, peaking just over 2x, now back to 1.72x.

mnyq.text: So each compute dollar brings back less. Who's getting paid?

1bt9.text: That's the next part of the story: where the money flows.

kv8c.text: TechCrunch writes that Anthropic pays SpaceX $1.25 billion a month for compute.

bthn.text: Plus multibillion-dollar deals with Nscale, Akamai and Volta.

a2ft.text: TechCrunch calls them neocloud, newer clouds, not the biggest cloud players.

qojx.text: It is: Anthropic Direct, its own compute.

d0x8.text: But TechCrunch thinks it can't keep up with demand.

ewlu.text: Where does the money end up?

bpnk.text: One example yesterday: chipmaker AMD reported Q3 results.

bh69.text: Its data center unit, selling server processors and AI chips, made $8.5 billion,

lvm1.text: AMD says Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle's cloud are already running work on its first Helios racks.

uczh.text: So some of Anthropic's money goes to AMD?

71n3.text: AMD only says they use it; no amounts given. That's what the company says.

tnh6.text: On the other side: companies that run models for others.

irzo.text: Fal, which hosts image and audio models, raised $1.3 billion; according to Bloomberg, at double its April valuation.

993g.text: Yes. TechCrunch cites sources: buying or renting compute is so pricey, margins stay thin.

ple4.text: Beyond chips, there's a deeper problem: power.

7yb2.text: TechCrunch, citing The New York Times: some AI data centers can't wait for the grid and use retired jet engines for power.

1pzu.text: Jet engines for power? That's intense.

zujv.text: In Northern Virginia, connecting 100 megawatts takes about 7 years, the IEA estimates.

egf8.text: With converted engines, an analyst says a data center can run in 24 months, but it's less efficient and dirtier.

41ju.text: Yes. Last month, Microsoft left its spot as anchor tenant at its UK data center.

vhse.text: Because the local utility said there won't be enough power until the early-to-mid 2030s.

531m.text: So money can't always buy compute.

x6k8.text: Chipmakers get orders; AMD is one.

0xed.text: Rent, pricier the more you rush.

5d9c.text: And what's holding everyone up is power.

mnya.text: The one rushing to buy: Anthropic itself. Revenue rose, compute spending rose faster.

jfi1.text: Does this affect what we pay for AI each month?

jie6.text: But every question you ask AI is a tiny line on this bill.

twnq.text: Chips and compute sound very Taiwan. Did the articles mention Taiwan?

twna.text: Honestly, none of today's pieces named a Taiwanese company. We won't force it.

2oz0.text: What we can say: AMD listed these in its risk factors.

vqdu.text: Plus memory supply, and relying on third-party makers.

d3b7.text: AMD didn't name them, so we won't. Whether Asia's supply chain is hit, today's sources don't say.

z6e4.text: One, the filing says compute and infrastructure spending will keep growing and be its biggest operating cost.

f2xh.text: Two, is this a blip or a long-term problem? TechCrunch thinks it's more like a short blip.

8qns.text: Three, if bond markets get nervous or local pushback grows, data center building may slow.

9reg.text: TechCrunch says if revenue grows fast enough, investors won't worry much about compute costs.

wv61.text: Back to that analyst. Monday's filing shows a company whose revenue soared, but compute takes more of every dollar.

9g8f.text: And that money flows to chips, clouds, and power that hasn't come yet.

u63w.text: We picked four quotes, all from the reports.

u7lu.text: First, Russell Brandom, the TechCrunch reporter who wrote it.

368b.text: He says margins are getting worse just when better margins could win over IPO investors.

gcwr.text: A Rystad Energy analyst told The New York Times: the key is getting power as fast as possible.

39tw.text: So engines first, even if less efficient.

dnrp.text: The third is about a name. The Verge reports that OpenAI's new announcement calls data centers compute campuses.

6kp4.text: New name, so neighbors stop protesting?

darw.text: Abre' Conner of the NAACP said renaming won't fix it.

xft7.text: OpenAI didn't answer The Verge's request for comment.

9fxy.text: Back to search. Adam Fry, head of ChatGPT's consumer products, says most people don't seem to mind ads in it.

svzk.text: We'll leave that one to you.

ud6a.text: Compute is company money; now, your money.

ihg8.text: Decrypt, citing Yonhap: North Korea denies hacking Binance.

xoeo.text: Wait, how much was taken from Binance?

hxx2.text: The FBI said last Saturday that North Korean hacking group TraderTraitor stole over $6 billion from Binance.

oclb.text: Decrypt reported earlier that about 2.85 billion has been frozen or seized.

wllv.text: Kim Jong Un's sister Kim Yo Jong called the US finding a serious political provocation.

7wne.text: More practical for users: two things Binance said. It says it has covered about 95 percent of stolen assets.

7nw3.text: It says holders of the top 10 tokens can use a zero-knowledge proof of the October 31 reserve snapshot

x68d.text: to check their balance is fully backed.

xzi2.text: Yes, the same kind of cryptography: proving something's true without revealing details.

plgd.text: Our advice: when an exchange has trouble, look for proof you can check yourself.

xk2j.text: The second story is also about saying no.

4eoy.text: A tokenized stock platform from OKX and ICE, the New York Stock Exchange's parent, now has 56 companies objecting.

jntm.text: Stocks turned into tokens on a blockchain and traded on blockchain platforms.

r5as.text: The six new ones include Tesla, SpaceX, Amazon and Netflix.

9uwp.text: Yes. Under the SEC's September innovation exemption, platforms notify them first.

fehm.text: If it objects in writing in 30 days, others' token versions can't be listed.

z8ye.text: Right. And per Decrypt, the platform is still in planning.

htqd.text: Last one, today's only Taiwan story.

fp84.text: Taiwan's regulator, the FSC, says it'll soon preview draft stablecoin issuer rules.

yfww.text: Crypto assets designed to be pegged to a legal currency.

lgku.text: Banks, financial holding firms, bank-invested companies, and others the FSC names.

cg1t.text: Non-banks need at least NT$300 million in paid-in capital.

edyq.text: They can issue stablecoins pegged one-to-one to the New Taiwan dollar or a single foreign currency.

lk0k.text: Reserves can't fall below what's in circulation.

bgww.text: Yes. Issuers must verify who subscribes and redeems, and get regular audits by accountants.

28m1.text: Not yet. Comments run 40 days from the day after notice; it starts with the Virtual Asset Service Act, undated by the Executive Yuan.

251t.text: Right, it's just a draft. And this segment doesn't discuss any coin prices.

vwey.text: OK, practical stuff. You said AI can fake calls. What can we do today?

1a87.text: This is the show's advice, not Google's instructions.

scma.text: One, if a familiar voice calls asking for money, hang up and call back on a number you saved.

gfdq.text: Yes. Sounding alike doesn't mean it's them.

9hi7.text: Two, on Android, open Settings, search "scam," and turn on any protection.

pvi0.text: Your phone may not have it yet.

9qnc.text: Three, Google says its game simulating common scams, Be Scam Ready, is in Taiwan already.

khjh.text: The new rating is for developers; our advice: set up parental controls on family iPhones yourself.

q7od.text: From real money to something a bit absurd: today's noise.

zokc.text: According to The Verge, several indie developers say Steam reviews took so long their games missed launch dates.

d4n5.text: Valve's own guidance: store page review usually takes 3 to 5 business days.

9sru.text: But a game called Food Devils was submitted October 12, was due out yesterday, and is still waiting.

05ct.text: Developers guess a flood of low-effort AI games clogged the queue.

5y7k.text: There are numbers: October's Steam Next Fest had 7,240 games, 65 percent more than June.

nxdo.text: One user counted that since Valve required labels, nearly half of new games say they use AI.

4nba.text: Valve later posted that reviews are behind, up to 12 business days. Blaming AI is still developers' guess.

4pwl.text: OK, this noise can wait in line.

7qsr.text: My take: the most important thing today is Anthropic's filing.

d9ls.text: Because it lays out the cost of running AI.

npwp.text: And it ties into chips, clouds and jet engines.

so1l.text: How this bill gets paid shapes the AI services you use.

kzi0.text: That's OpenAI; reports don't link the two. I just find them worth reading together.

z02r.text: Honestly, I'm not sure. TechCrunch sees a short blip; we'll see next quarter's numbers.

k0ch.text: Full stories are on Mokaair; links in the description.

qans.text: Back to today's topic: most of the money went to compute, and bought in a hurry.

lvsq.text: Pay more, or watch ads? Tell us.

lkby.text: Want the highlights daily? Subscribe to Tech Signal. Signal received.
